subject: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Hi Alex  great speaking with you earlier. Thanks for the detailed product overview; I wanted to capture the key follow-ups and propose a concrete POC plan so we can get to a kickoff quickly.

Recap / proposed success criteria (please confirm or edit):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference < 300ms for the core low-latency path.
- Cost: per-inference token cost <= $0.002 (baseline target for evaluation).
- Accuracy/quality: top-line intent-recognition F1 >= 0.92 on the 10k sample set you mentioned.
- Stability: no errors or 5xxs under your peak burst for > 30 minutes.

POC scope & timeline (proposed):
- 2-week trial: Week 1 onboarding + smoke tests, Week 2 load / quality evaluation.
- Kickoff: Tue Jan 19 (30-45m)  technical kickoff with your eng + our SE (Marissa).
- Deliverables: pre-configured workload runner, evaluation script, and a short POC report with key metrics.

Workload intake items we need from you (I attached a CSV template):
- Average RPS: what you expect in steady-state.
- Peak burst RPS and burst duration.
- Concurrency (simultaneous sessions/threads).
- Typical prompt token length and average completion token length.
- Sample payloads / 100-1k sample requests (sanitized).
- Any PII or redaction constraints.

Our initial suggestions (subject to your numbers):
- Start on hosted Redwood API; if you need isolation we can scope Dedicated capacity during the POC.
- Model: redwood-3.1-xl (quantized)  Marissa will confirm fit for latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Batching target: 32 tokens/requests; max request token cap recommended: 512.

Next steps:
1) Alex  fill the attached workload-intake.csv and send a small sample data export (or confirm when procurement can sign any required MSA).
2) Marissa  to propose a concrete test plan and initial infra config by EOD Wed.
3) Ben  schedule kickoff for Jan 19 if that works for Alex.

Attachments: poc-plan-template.docx, workload-intake.csv (template)

Thanks  excited to get started.

Best,
Ben

Ben  thanks for the recap, that matches my notes. Quick answers below (happy to expand):

POC success criteria (our priorities):
- Quality: intent-recognition F1 >= 0.92 on our labeled 10k sample.
- Latency: 95p < 350ms (we can tolerate slightly higher initially).
- Cost: looking to validate cost targets vs our current provider  lower is better but quality comes first.

Workload profile (initial):
- Average steady-state RPS: ~12 RPS (globalized traffic but US-heavy).
- Peak burst RPS: up to ~120 RPS for short spikes (1-5 minutes during batch jobs).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~8, occasional spikes to 25.
- Token lengths: average prompt ~80 tokens, average completion ~120 tokens.
- Test dataset size: plan to run 10k requests across a mix of short/long prompts.

We attached a small sample (sanitized)  sample-traffic.jsonl  and filled a few fields in your CSV. Procurement (procurement@fintechlabs.com) is looped for contracts.

Question: for our spike pattern, would you recommend starting on hosted or go dedicated from day 1? Also curious about data-retention and PII handling for the sample dataset.

Happy to join Jan 19 kickoff.

Alex
Head of Product | Fintech Labs, Inc.
ajohnson@fintechlabs.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Hi Alex  thanks for the quick answers and sample file. I pulled your numbers into the intake template and sketched an initial POC test plan below.

Proposed POC test plan (2 weeks):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): exchange sample data, sign minimal NDA/MSA if needed, set up Redwood dev keys.
- Week 1: onboarding + smoke tests (validate auth, sample runs, small batch).
- Week 2: load testing + quality evaluation (run full 10k dataset, measure latency/cost/accuracy).

Evaluation metrics and how we'll measure:
- Latency: 95th/99th percentiles measured by our load runner + your telemetry.
- Quality: run your labeled 10k set through fixed model + scoring harness (we'll produce confusion matrix + F1).
- Stability: error rate and successful request ratio under peak burst scenarios.
- Cost: token accounting during the 10k test run and extrapolated monthly unit economics.

Initial infra/config recommendations based on your numbers:
- Hosted API is fine for a first POC  it's low-friction. For your short burst to 120 RPS, Redwood's autoscaling should handle it, but if you need guaranteed headroom and private networking we can provision a small Dedicated pool (T-shirt size: 1x A100-equivalent) during the trial. We can size more precisely after early smoke tests.
- Model config: redwood-3.1-xl (float16 / 4-bit quant), batch target 32, max request tokens 512.
- Concurrency throttles: soft limit at 25 concurrent reqs; we'll set worker pools to smooth bursts.

Data & compliance notes:
- Please confirm whether the sample file contains any regulated PII. If so, we recommend anonymizing before upload. We can sign an RTPA if needed and enable stricter retention on the POC logs.

Next steps (owners):
- Alex: confirm POC kick-off time Jan 19 and whether you prefer hosted-first vs dedicated baseline. (Alex)
- Ben: coordinate commercial / MSA and confirm any credit / trial terms. (Ben)
- Marissa: deliver the test harness + README by Wed EOD and a concrete Dedicated sizing estimate after initial smoke. (Marissa)

Link: I created a shared folder with the POC plan and scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bPOCshare

Thanks  we'll be ready for Jan 19 kickoff.

Best,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
